title: Detection of Continuum Submillimeter Emission Associated with Candidate Protoplanets
question: Is there sub-mm continuum emission associated with the PDS 70 planets b and c, and what dust mass would a circumplanetary disk need to explain it?

what.value: Planet masses, luminosities, orbital radii, accretion rates (Table 1)

evidence.quote: We assume a stellar luminosity $L_\star=0.36 L_\odot$ (cite: Muller2018)
a dust opacity of 3.5 cm$^{2}$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: Keppler2019)

recipe.method: Phase self-cal of short-baseline data, then of combined data; tclean imaging at several robust values

recipe.goal: Subtract symmetric ring to expose c_smm
recipe.method: Visibility-space shift, deprojection, azimuthal average subtraction, re-imaging
2D Gaussian fits relative to disk center from continuum core and CO Keplerian rotation center
Grid of CPD models (Isella 2014) with temperature from viscous heating plus planet and stellar irradiation, matched to 106 uJy
key_parameters: T_irr,* 20-80 K; mu=0.1; Sigma ∝ r^-1; Rout 0.3-3 au
assumptions: kappa=3.5 cm2/g; gas-to-dust 100; CPD inclination equals circumstellar disk

evidence.quote: PDS 70 c$_{smm}$ has a peak intensity of 106$\pm$19 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ (snr $\sim5.6$)

answer_key.quantity: Offset of b_smm from PDS 70 b
CPD dust mass of PDS 70 c

evidence.quote: dust mass between $2\times10^{-3}$ M$_\Earth$ and $4.2 \times 10^{-3}$ M$_\Earth$
and a flux density of 177 mJy
the measured aspect ratio implies a disk inclination of 52$^\circ$

not_stated_but_needed: Cleaning threshold, mask and scales for the robust 0.3 and 2 final images
Spectral windows and line-free channels used for the continuum
Flux calibrator and corrected flux value for the 2016 data
Fit procedure and errors for the 2D Gaussian source fits
Details of the CPD flux model grid (inner radius, inclination used numerically)
score_reason: Public data, script released and detailed self-cal; some final imaging and model details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, released script, numeric results.
